en: The Essential Teachings of Linji, Written by the Monk Huihong of Mingbai Hermitage.
Chan Master Fenyang Shao addressed the assembly, saying: "The former sages said that a single phrase must embody the three mysteries, and each mystery..."
Within this, one must possess the three essentials. What are these phrases of the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials? Understand them well! Each of you should reflect for yourselves:

have you attained a state of stability yet? When the ancients of old went on pilgrimage, if they heard a single kōan (in-yuan) that they did not clearly understand, they would immediately lose their appetite for food and find no peace in sleep until they had urgently resolved it. How could they possibly...
It is not for a minor matter that the Greatly Awakened Elder appeared in the world for the sake of the one great cause and condition.
Consider how those who have traveled on pilgrimage since ancient times did not do so to roam mountains, play with the waters, or view the splendors of prefectures and capitals;

every bit of clothing and every morsel of food were for the purpose that their sacred minds had not yet attained penetration. Therefore, they hurried along on pilgrimage to resolve profound mysteries and transmit the teachings.

To propagate [the Dharma], one must inquire extensively of those with prior knowledge and draw near to those of high virtue. This is done, indeed, to continue the lamp of the Buddha’s mind and to perpetuate the lineage of the Buddhas;
to honor the ancestral seeds of the Sage and to guide those of future capacity; to benefit oneself and others, never forgetting the traces of the past.
Is there anyone present now who would offer an assessment? If there is, come forth and let us deliberate together. A monk asked: "What is it to provide guidance?"
The phrase for beginners: Question: "What is it? Answer: "You are a wandering monk. Again he asked: "What is the phrase that distinguishes a patch-robed monk?
Answer: "The sun rises in the west at dawn. Again he asked: "What is the phrase where the true command is put into effect? Answer:
"Bringing it from a thousand miles away to present to the old face. Again he asked: "What is the phrase that establishes heaven and earth? Answer: "The North."
"In the land of Kuru, there is long-grained rice; those who eat it have neither anger nor joy. The Master said, "I shall use these four turning words to test the monks of the world.
As soon as you come forward, I will have tested you. A monk asked, "What is the place where a student exerts effort?
He replied, "Jiaozhou strikes the Great Image. The monk asked, "What is the place where a student turns about? He replied, [as before].
[The Master] said, "In Shanfu, one waters the iron ox. [A monk] asked, "What is the point of intimacy for a student?
[The Master] replied, "In Xihe, one plays with the lion. The Master said, "If a person understands these three phrases, they have already mastered the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan).

There are further words of the Three Essentials (Sanyao) that remain; it is essential to grasp them, for this is no trivial matter. I shall provide a verse for the assembly on the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials: The Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials.
The matter is difficult to distinguish. When one attains the meaning, forgetting the words, the Way becomes easy to approach. A single phrase clearly encompasses the myriad phenomena;
on the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh. Do you understand? If you understand in such a way, you are not a monk of impetuous temperament.
How, then, should you understand? Again, he raised the words of the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan), saying: "Do you understand the timing of the Three Mysteries? You must understand them directly."

Grasp the essential meaning of the ancients, and then your own mind will become clear; you will further attain the power of adaptive transformation, and your own self-reliant enjoyment will be inexhaustible.
This is called the Buddha of Self-Enjoyment. Without following the teachings of others, you will immediately recognize your own living reality.
Thus Nanquan said, "When I was eighteen, I understood how to manage my livelihood. A monk then asked, "The ancients [said] ten..."
The eighth [case] concerns understanding how to make one's livelihood. I do not yet know what kind of livelihood this is. He replied:
"Two water-buffaloes with no rings on their twin horns. He further said: "If you wish to attain clarity regarding this, you must first grasp the essential purport of the Three Mysteries;
only then will you be able to enjoy it without hindrance, bringing joy to yourself and fulfilling your life’s purpose as a true man."

Do not allow yourself to be self-defeating; do not let your engagement with affairs be obstructed. Since that [state] provides no benefit or salvation, I shall recite for you a verse on all these matters:
The First Mystery: The Dharma-realm is vast and boundless; The myriad phenomena and all things Are entirely present within the mirror, complete. The Second Mystery:
The World-Honored One questioned Ānanda, who replied according to the facts: "The capacity of the vessel determines its shape and size.
This is the third of the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan), which directly emerges before the Ancient Sovereign. Beyond the four propositions and the hundred negations, Master Lü asked Fenggan:
"This is a verse on the Three Mysteries; what is the essential meaning of the Three Mysteries? You must resolve this with clear discernment; do not merely..."
To thus vainly interpret this in the air, saying, "I have personally attended upon the Master; he explained it to me," is to speak empty falsehoods to deceive others.
You will have a day when you eat iron rods; do not say I did not warn you. Furthermore, while picking chrysanthemums, he said to the assembly:
"Golden flowers spread across the earth; jade stamens receive the heavens. The bright sun hangs in the sky, illuminating heaven and earth with its radiance. Clouds...
Vapor rises to form dew, which then condenses into frost. This does not violate the principle of benefiting all things. Bring forth a single word of the Way—is there anyone who can speak it?
If you cannot speak it, there is a speck of dust in your eye; you must remove it before you may succeed. Therefore, Fengxue said:
"If you establish even a single atom of dust, the state will flourish while the village elders frown; if you do not establish even a single atom of dust, the state will perish."
The wild old man is at ease here; if you understand this clearly, you are not the *ācārya*, but entirely this old monk.

If you do not understand this clearly, this old monk is precisely the *ācārya*. The *ācārya* and this old monk can both enlighten the people of the world, and they can also blind the people of the world.
Do you wish to know who this old monk and the *ācārya* are? [He] pats his knee and says: "Right here."
"This is the *ācārya*. Here is this old monk. Now ask the various *upādhyāyas*: Are this old monk and the *ācārya* the same or different?
If you say they are the same, then the *upādhyāya* remains the *upādhyāya* and the old monk remains the old monk.
If you say they are different, yet you also say that the old monk is precisely the *ācārya*. If you can clearly understand this within a single phrase,"
There are the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials; guest and host are clearly distinguished. One’s lifelong task is accomplished and the quest for the Way is concluded.
Thus Yongjia said: "To grind one's bones to powder would not suffice as recompense; a single phrase, when realized, transcends billions. He also said:
"One day, the two head monks of Linji’s two halls met face-to-face and simultaneously let out a shout. A monk asked Linji, 'Is there still a distinction between guest and host?'"
Wu. He replied, "The roles of guest and host are clearly distinct. The Master then composed a verse: "The two hall heads are both masters;
The principles within them are distinct and clear. Guest and host are as vivid as a mirror; The patriarch points out the flower in one's eye. Master Wu-jin said to me:
"Fenyang was the direct fifth-generation descendant of Linji; he is the one revered by scholars throughout the world."
Looking up, I observe that their grand, overarching principles consist solely of the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials.
Now, those within their dharma lineage all claim that the words regarding the "establishment of the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials for a single period" are of no benefit to the Way;

they maintain that merely not giving rise to divergent views toward any phenomena, but remaining entirely ordinary, is itself the intention of the Patriarch. Is this teaching correct? I said, "Layman, have you heard of it?"
I said, "If one explains it so as to be clearly understood, how could one still doubt the guiding principles of Fenyang? He replied, "I have indeed doubted them, yet I have not reached a resolution.
I said, "This is precisely why the Three Mysteries (Sanxuan) and the Three Essentials (Sanyao) were established.

What is meant by 'a single phrase contains the Three Mysteries' and 'within each Mystery there are the Three Essentials,' and the presence of both Mysteries and Essentials, is that for all sentient beings, the ocean of feverish afflictions..."
It is the banner of the Dharma that is intrinsically cool, serene, and extinguished. The raising of this banner is like a drum smeared with lethal poison:
when it is struck, all who hear it die; however, those who hear it from afar die later. Unless one meets an untimely death, even upon hearing it, one does not die.
When Linji was still alive, those such as Xinghua, Sansheng, Baoshou, and the Venerable Ding heard his teaching and died;
even now, more than a hundred years later, there are still those who have awakened to his essential meaning—they are precisely those who died after him.

As for those whom various Dharma lineages claim were of no benefit to the Way, they are those who did not die a "horizontal" death. The ancestral school’s style stands like a wall ten thousand fathoms high, yet the son...
Sun Wei feared this. He delighted in promoting easy and level paths; this is what is called the gradual decline of the Way of the Dharma.

It is like those who wear the robes and caps of the Confucian tradition yet disparage and alter the *Xici* (Appended Phrases) of the *Book of Changes*; even a child of three feet would laugh at them. Linji merely said:
"Within a single phrase are contained the Three Mysteries; within each Mystery are contained the Three Essentials. There are simply Mysteries and Essentials. At first...
I have never referred to them as the "mystery within the phrase," the "mystery within the meaning," or the "mystery within the essence.
The ancient Abbot [Zhaozhou] mistakenly identified Xuedou’s three phrases as the Three Mysteries; thus, he merely divided them into the Three Mysteries while omitting the Three Essentials.
That the monastic communities accepted this without deeming it erroneous is truly lamentable. Xuedou said: "The continuous flow of true permanence is the Dharma of equality."
However, using words to dispel words and using principle to pursue principle results in clarifying what precedes while leaving what follows obscure;

this is merely the measure of partial realization of the Dharma-body, wherein there are no phrases that transcend the conventional. One dies beneath the words unless one knows the measure of transcending them.
Thus, one is not driven by the demon of the mind. Upon entering into the hand [of the master], it is immediately transformed and brought to full realization.
This is called "penetrating the Great Way," wherein one does not abide in ordinary views; this is the first phrase. The ancients called it the "mystery within the phrase.

It involves turning the mechanism and shifting the position, possessing mastery over life and death, granting or withholding as appropriate, and traversing birth and death to extensively benefit all beings, thereby attaining a state of complete liberation.
The realm of form, desire, love, and views—this is the second phrase. The ancients called it the "mystery within the mind": it illuminates the yin and penetrates the yang;
it is vast and pervasive throughout the *sāhasra-lokadhātu*. The great function of the single true essence manifests before one; its responsive transformations are without fixed direction.

It is entirely functioning and entirely non-functioning; entirely arising and entirely non-arising. As a skillful means, it is termed the "gate of compassionate concentration. This is the third phrase.
The ancients called this "the mystery within the essence. Master Yuan of Fushan also said, "The 'mystery within the mind' does not refer to the mind of conscious thought.
The ancients are not worth discussing, and Yuan was likewise deluded; I cannot fail to distinguish this. Wujin nodded in agreement. He further said:
"I recently heard from Xie Shizhi that the monk Jiancheng of Wu possesses great insight and has personally studied under Ciming; he is truly one of those who 'point directly at the chest.
He belongs to the same lineage as Yangqi and Daowu, and when receiving people, he frequently cites the 'Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality' of Fenyang;
I wish to hear his explanation. I replied, "The Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality and the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are one and the same."
The pivotal point. Fenyang said: "One who expounds the Dharma must possess the Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality.

If one does not possess the Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality, one cannot distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, nor differentiate between the monastic and the lay; thus, one cannot serve as the eyes for devas and humans to adjudicate right from wrong.
It would be like a bird flying through the sky with broken wings, or an arrow shot at a target with a severed string. Because the string is severed, the shooting [fails]."
If the feathers are broken, the void cannot be flown through; if the string is strong and the feathers are firm, the void is pierced through entirely.
What is this "Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality"? I shall point them out for you, venerable elders: first, identity of substance; second, identity of the Great Matter.
Third, identical in shared practice; fourth, identical in true wisdom; fifth, identical in universal pervasiveness; sixth, identical in full completion; seventh, identical in gain and loss;
eighth, identical in life and death; ninth, identical in the roar of the voice; tenth, identical in attaining entry. It is further asked:

With what kind of person is one identical in attaining entry? With whom is one identical in the roar of the voice? What is this identity in life and death? What thing is identical in gain and loss? A.
Which one is identical in its fullness? What is identical in its pervasive universality? Who possesses identical true wisdom?
Who is able to participate in this total identity? Which one is identical in the Great Matter? What thing is identical in its single substance? Is there anyone who can point it out?
Those who can point it out do not begrudge their compassion; those who cannot point it out have yet to possess the eye for study. You must resolutely prepare yourself for this. You must desire it!

To recognize right from wrong is to see one’s own face as it is right now. Yet, in this present Dharma-gate, the monastic communities are filled with fear and dread, having no desire to hear it. Why is this so?
It is because those in all quarters cherish only superficial, intellectual understanding, clinging to it without wavering;

they wish only to transmit their views and do not believe in actual awakening. Even if Fenyang were to be reborn today and personally analyze these matters for them, he would still consider such views to be incorrect. Long ago, Ānanda...
It was difficult to walk about at night. Hearing a youth reciting a verse of the Buddha, he said:

"If a person lives for a hundred years, yet is not skillful as a crane by a marsh, it is not as good as living for a single day and attaining decisive understanding. Ānanda approached him and instructed him, saying, "He is not unskillful regarding the devices of the Buddhas;
he is no mere crane by a marsh. When the youth returned and reported this to his teacher, the teacher laughed and said, "Ānanda is old and senile."
"It is so. You should take my words as correct. How does the teaching on the three mysteries and ten wisdoms before the students of today differ from this?
Thereupon, Wu Jin sighed in admiration and said, "Indeed, how could there not be expedient means regarding its essential purport?
I then composed a verse, saying: "The ten wisdoms share the same reality; their true face is complete. Among them, one wisdom is the root source. If [one] greatly..."
I saw the Old Man of Fenyang, who split the Three Mysteries into two sides. I further asked: "Are the four types of guest and host also Dharma-gates established by Linji? I replied:
"The Tathāgatas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations have forged the crucibles and hammers that refine away the emotional views of ordinary and sage;
it is not only Linji who employs them. For instance, there was Longshan Benjian meeting Mazu, and Dongshan Liangjie."

When the Chan Master first traveled to seek teachers, he journeyed together with his senior companion, Master Mi. Passing beneath Longshan in Changsha, they saw vegetable leaves floating down the stream.
Huaike turned back to gaze at the deep and exquisite mountain peaks and said to Mi, "There must be a hidden practitioner here."
They proceeded along the stream for about ten *li*. There was an elderly monk who appeared extremely emaciated. Placing his hands upon his forehead, he called out, "There is no path here;
how have you all come to this place? Prajñā said, "Setting aside the matter of there being no path for a moment, from where did you yourself enter, Master of the Hermitage?
The monk replied, "I have never been a wandering monk (*yun-shui*). Prajñā asked, "How long has the Master lived on this mountain? He replied, "Not in terms of spring or autumn."
Sheshan said, "Did you, Master, dwell here first, or did this mountain dwell here first? He replied, "I do not know. Sheshan asked, "Why do you not know?
He replied, "I have never had anyone or any god come to me. Sheshan asked, "What principle have you realized that allows you to dwell on this mountain in such a manner?"

He said, "I see the clay oxen fighting as they enter the sea; even until now, there has been no news. Jia then stepped down from the platform and struck him with his staff. He asked, "What is the guest within the host? He replied, "Green mountains shroud white clouds. He asked again, "What is the host within the host? He replied, "Never leaving the door for all one's life. He asked again, "How far apart are the host and the guest? He replied: The clay oxen fight and enter the sea, To this very day, no news has come. Jia descended from the platform and struck him. "What is the guest within the host? "Green mountains shroud white clouds. "How is the host within the host? "Never leaving the door for all one's life. "How far apart are the host and the guest? "The distance between the two is ten thousand miles. "Where do the host and the guest meet? "The meeting place is the single road. "What is the meaning of 'one road'? "One road is the path of the sages. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the sages'? "The path of the sages is the path of the ordinary person. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the ordinary person'? "The path of the ordinary person is the path of the Buddha. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Buddha'? "The path of the Buddha is the path of the patriarchs. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the patriarchs'? "The path of the patriarchs is the path of the mind-ground. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the mind-ground'? "The path of the mind-ground is the path of the Dharma-body. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Dharma-body'? "The path of the Dharma-body is the path of emptiness. "What is the meaning of 'the path of emptiness'? "The path of emptiness is the path of non-attainment. "What is the meaning of 'the path of non-attainment'? "The path of non-attainment is the path of liberation. "What is the meaning of 'the path of liberation'? "The path of liberation is the path of Nirvana. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Nirvana'? "The path of Nirvana is the path of the Great Way. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Great Way'? "The path of the Great Way is the path of the Middle Way. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Middle Way'? "The path of the Middle Way is the path of the One Vehicle. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the One Vehicle'? "The path of the One Vehicle is the path of the Three Vehicles. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Three Vehicles'? "The path of the Three Vehicles is the path of the Twelve Divisions of Scripture. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Twelve Divisions of Scripture'? "The path of the Twelve Divisions of Scripture is the path of the Eightfold Path. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Eightfold Path'? "The path of the Eightfold Path is the path of the Four Noble Truths. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Four Noble Truths'? "The path of the Four Noble Truths is the path of the Six Paramitas. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Six Paramitas'? "The path of the Six Paramitas is the path of the Ten Stages. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Ten Stages'? "The path of the Ten Stages is the path of the Five Eyes. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Five Eyes'? "The path of the Five Eyes is the path of the Six Supernatural Powers. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Six Supernatural Powers'? "The path of the Six Supernatural Powers is the path of the Three Bodies. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Three Bodies'? "The path of the Three Bodies is the path of the One Mind. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the One Mind'? "The path of the One Mind is the path of the True Suchness. "What is the meaning of 'the path of True Suchness'? "The path of True Suchness is the path of the Unconditioned. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Unconditioned'? "The path of the Unconditioned is the path of the Ultimate Reality. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Ultimate Reality'? "The path of Ultimate Reality is the path of the Great Void. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Great Void'? "The path of the Great Void is the path of the Great Peace. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Peace'? "The path of Great Peace is the path of the Great Awakening. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Awakening'? "The path of Great Awakening is the path of the Great Enlightenment. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Enlightenment'? "The path of Great Enlightenment is the path of the Great Liberation. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Liberation'? "The path of Great Liberation is the path of the Great Return. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Great Return'? "The path of the Great Return is the path of the Great Completion. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Completion'? "The path of Great Completion is the path of the Great Perfection. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Perfection'? "The path of Great Perfection is the path of the Great Emptiness. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Emptiness'? "The path of Great Emptiness is the path of the Great Non-existence. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Non-existence'? "The path of Great Non-existence is the path of the Great Absence. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Absence'? "The path of Great Absence is the path of the Great Silence. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Silence'? "The path of Great Silence is the path of the Great Stillness. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Stillness'? "The path of Great Stillness is the path of the Great Tranquility. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Tranquility'? "The path of Great Tranquility is the path of the Great Peace. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Peace'? "The path of Great Peace is the path of the Great Bliss. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Bliss'? "The path of Great Bliss is the path of the Great Joy. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Joy'? "The path of Great Joy is the path of the Great Laughter. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Laughter'? "The path of Great Laughter is the path of the Great Smile. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Great Smile'? "The path of the Great Smile is the path of the Great Sigh. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Great Sigh'? "The path of the Great Sigh is the path of the Great Cry. "What is the meaning of 'the path of the Great Cry'? "The path of the Great Cry is the path of the Great Weeping. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Weeping'? "The path of Great Weeping is the path of the Great Anguish. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Anguish'? "The path of Great Anguish is the path of the Great Suffering. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Suffering'? "The path of Great Suffering is the path of the Great Pain. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Pain'? "The path of Great Pain is the path of the Great Torment. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Torment'? "The path of Great Torment is the path of the Great Despair. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Despair'? "The path of Great Despair is the path of the Great Hopelessness. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Hopelessness'? "The path of Great Hopelessness is the path of the Great Helplessness. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Helplessness'? "The path of Great Helplessness is the path of the Great Abandonment. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Abandonment'? "The path of Great Abandonment is the path of the Great Renunciation. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Renunciation'? "The path of Great Renunciation is the path of the Great Detachment. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Detachment'? "The path of Great Detachment is the path of the Great Dispassion. "What is the meaning of 'the path of Great Dispassion'? "The path of Great Dis
"Ripples upon the waters of the Yangtze River. He further asked, "When host and guest meet, what words are exchanged? Baizhang replied, "The azure wind brushes against the white sun.
Guishan bowed twice and requested to take him as his teacher. The old monk laughed and said: "I have always dwelt in a three-bay thatched cottage;

A single path of divine light leaves all phenomena at rest. Do not come to judge me with notions of right and wrong; In this floating life, artificial analysis is irrelevant. At this, [Guishan] attained realization.
He set fire to his own hermitage and entered deep into the layered peaks. Later, when Guishan (Jia) resided on the mountain, he asked a monk, "Who is this master of yours?
The monk replied, "The one currently responding to you. Guishan looked up and sighed, saying, "This is what is called the business of the horse behind and the donkey in front.
How can you recognize this as your own self? This is a portent that the Buddha-dharma will sink into oblivion."—Recorded by a guest.
If even the "Master of the Middle" has not yet been clarified, how much less so the "Master of Masters"? A monk asked, "What is the Master of Masters? Jia said, "Try saying it yourself.
The monk said, "If one can say it, that is the Master of Guests; what then is the Master of Masters?
Jia remained silent for a long while and then said, "I do not refuse to tell you, but continuity is also very difficult. In my view, this was the intention of the old monk Longshan.
It was like Xiao He’s recognition of Han Xin—how could there be any fixed method for it? Yet Master Jia’s discourse was like Huo Guang’s conduct at court;
his every advance and retreat possessed a disciplined measure. Alas! It is certain that those of later generations cannot see the full greatness of the ancients.
One might suspect that Master Jia also kept the "Lord of Lords" within his breast. Once, I visited Linchuan.
Juefan was on friendly terms with Zhu Shiying. Shortly thereafter, the Elder of Shanglan arrived at Shanggai and said to Shiying, "I have heard that Juefan is skilled in poetry;
as for Chan, even his own master would still err, so how much more so his disciples? Shiying laughed and said:
"Can you, Master, examine this? Shanglan replied, "Yes. After one day had passed, they went together to Shushan and ate at the home of a relative.
Shanglan drew a circle on the table with his hand and said to me, "On the top of a sutra scroll, there must be characters written; what is the meaning of this?
I also drew a circle with a horizontal line through it and said, "This is its meaning. Shanglan was struck dumb with astonishment. I [acted] for him...
He composed a verse, saying: "By means of characters it is not formed; eight is not it. The Dharma-body sleeps soundly, with nothing to obstruct or disturb.
A patch-robed monk faces it directly yet does not know its name; Before a crowd of hundreds, one cannot call it forth. Shanglan returned and presented this to Shiying.
Shiying clapped his hands and said, "Who is this poet-monk? Is he also able to understand the meaning of characters? Thereupon, they went together to see Fenyang making a calf.
The Ox Gāthā says: "Having a head but no horns—truly a cause for lamentation; Through a hundred kalpas, one cannot escape this Master.
Neither ordinary nor sage can fully comprehend it; Its manifest appearance is somewhat present. I said to Shiying:
"This gāthā is also an exegesis on the meaning of my name. Shiying asked me: "The Avataṃsaka Sūtra says: 'The Rishi Vimala held onto goodness...'"
Sudhana. At that moment, Sudhana saw his own body dwelling within worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;

he went before as many Buddhas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields and beheld those buddha-fields and their assemblies, with the Buddhas adorned by various marks and signs of excellence, even for periods spanning hundreds of thousands of billions of unspeakable numbers of buddha-field atoms.
For many kalpas... until at last that rishi released the hand of the youth Sudhana. Immediately, he saw his own body returned to its original place.
How is this section of meaning to be explained? I say: it is all a matter of mental imagery (*nimitta*).

At the very moment one grasps the hand—that is, when entering the contemplation of the Dharma—one sees that self and other are not separated by even a hair’s breadth, and from beginning to end, nothing has shifted.
One should maintain mindfulness; when the hands are released, that is precisely the moment of emerging from meditative absorption. Yongming said:

"Thus we know that without moving from one's original station, the lands near and far are clearly manifest; without a single thought shifting, the duration of time—whether extended or condensed—is vividly present.
The World-Honored One used the lotus as a metaphor, yet none in the world have understood it; I alone have understood it. Indeed, when the lotus is about to open its flowers, [the petals]...
Within the seed there is already the sprout; within the sprout there is already the stalk. Thus, the effect exists within the cause, and the cause exists within the effect.
The three periods of time are simultaneous. As the seeds are distributed, they further belong to one another; their continuity is unbroken, and the ten directions are not separated.
He asked again: The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* says: "The World-Honored One, before the assembly of all beings, manifested great supernormal power and extended his broad and long tongue."

Regarding this mark: from the highest reaches of the Brahma-world, it is extremely difficult to reconcile [the physical reality with the phenomenon]. Yet those who explain it say: "The Buddha’s voice is profound and subtle, heard everywhere; as it transcends both the holy and the mundane, his tongue is broad, long, and extends upward beyond the Brahma-world. What do you think of this explanation? "This is likely what is called 'generating understanding according to the words'; it is not the intention of the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One. Guishan said:
'When the sentiments of ordinary and sage are exhausted, the essence reveals true permanence; when principle and phenomena are non-dual, that is the Buddha of Suchness.
Yet students are unable to savor these words deeply; they merely grasp at their own conjectures. It is like a group of blind men feeling an elephant, each acting according to what they have touched."
Thus, if one were to take only the trunk, tail, hooves, waist, or tusks as representative of the elephant, the whole elephant would remain hidden.
The *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* states: "Because it is non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption—this is true permanence (*tathatā*).

This true permanence is not a fixed, singular entity that stands apart, immutable and indestructible. That the mark of the tongue reaches up to the Brahma-world—how could this be sought through ordinary emotional cognition?

Ah! When the Tang monk Xuanzang arrived in Western India, he met the Master of Śāstras Śīlabhadra. At that time, Śīlabhadra was already one hundred and six years old and was venerated by all as the "Treasury of the True Dharma" (Saddharmakośa).
After Xuanzang had paid his respects, Śīlabhadra invited him to sit and asked where he had come from.
He replied, "I have come from the land of China, wishing to study the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* and other treatises. Thereupon, Śīlabhadra shed tears and called to his disciples.
Bodhiruci pointed and said to him, "What do you think of my previous dream, disciple? Xuanzang replied to the Master, saying, "Three years ago, the Upādhyāya fell gravely ill;
it was as if someone were cutting open his belly with a knife. He wished to die by fasting. At night, he dreamed of a man with a golden body who said:
'Do not loathe your own body. In the past you were noble, but recently you have harmed many living beings.'"
"You should now repent and reproach yourself. What benefit is there in exhausting yourself? A monk from the land of China has come here to study the Dharma;
he is already on his way and shall arrive in three years. Bestow the Dharma upon him, and as he in turn propagates it, your transgressions will naturally be extinguished.
I am Mañjuśrī, and thus I have come to inform you. Although the Upādhyāya’s illness had already persisted for three years, the Ācārya indeed...
"Your arrival is a fulfillment of the signs from my previous dream. You have encountered many hardships throughout your life; these were likely due to karmic obstacles from past lives.

Upon hearing the words of Mañjuśrī, you resolved to bestow the Dharma upon others, whereby your transgressions naturally ceased. It is for this reason that I have conceived the intention to compile the essential instructions of the Buddhas and Patriarchs."
I wish to bestow this upon others and thereby extinguish my own long-standing obstacles; there is no other pursuit.
(End of the Linji School’s Essential Teachings)
